source.scope: in-world entity rendering: players (type 0/1), monsters (type 3..0x31), NPC (type 0x32), ground items/deco, effects. Window-relative coords; client 800x600.

conclusion: The world entity render pipeline is fully closed statically: the frame function (0x41BCB7) runs 0x419D40 (world sort pass -> four y-sorted painter arrays root+0x154 entities / +0x2E4 effects / +0x474 ground deco / +0x604 ground items) then 0x41C450 (ground/tile pass over the camera-visible tile range), which per visible tile drives ground-item draw 0x41C860, ground-deco draw 0x41CA20, per-tile entity draw 0x41CBD0 and effect draw 0x41CD50. Per-tile entity draw dispatches on the type byte [entity+0x88]: types 0/1 (players) and 0x32 (NPC) are blitted via vtable+0x7C = 0x40B2C0 (world->screen sx/sy formulas into [e+0xE4]/[e+0xE8]), which resolves the WIL lib by element and blits with render-mode flag resolution (0x404DA0) and the 0x404E10/0x461ED0 blit family. Monsters (types 3..0x31, incl. type 3 per raw 0x41CD1C table case 1) and types 2 are blitted via the per-entity tick chain: vtable+0x1C = 0x40ADD0 -> vtable+0x20 = 0x40AFD0 (frame advance) -> vtable+0x18 = 0x40A2B0 (state-machine dispatch 0x456270 state word -> per-state slots vtable+0x44..0x6C, e.g. 0x4070C0) -> painter 0x405630 (leaf; 10 direct call sites, never in a vtable). Element->WIL binding and the animation frame formulas are static (type 0 -> M-Hum slot 71, type 1 -> WM-Hum slot 76, type 3 race<2000 -> 0x58+race/10, race>=2000 -> 0x87+(race-2000)/100, type 0x32 -> NPC slot 128; horse selector byte 0x629CF=0x57 -> slot 87). Remaining unknowns are runtime-capture only (entity-list head insertion, DB frame-table contents, per-monster blit ordering).
